A: **Two options:** Solo queue vs Fault Tables. **Tables win.** Sort arrivals by symptom—dead, intermittent, mechanical—into three chair rings of four; electrician rotates 15 minutes per ring, narrating one fix while three mirror steps on their own items. Example: dead-lamp ring tests fuses together, each visitor meters next person's plug. **Test:** next week count visitors who diagnose a stranger's item unaided; Tables should double queue's rate.
B: **Two options:** Mirror energy vs Time-share. **Time-share wins.** Pre-agree clock slots: on quarter-hours one plays sparse drone under volume cap while other takes melody and crowd; roles swap every 15 minutes. Livelier end always pulls wanderers, then hands them back. Example: 8:00 Ana solos, Ben hums; 8:15 reverse. **Test:** tally minutes each case gains zero coins; time-share should halve simultaneous starvation versus both-busking, with total tips steady.
C: **Two options:** Shuffle-bag random vs Numbered ledger. **Ledger wins.** Each drop gets sequential number, duplicate stub for dropper; tapes play oldest-first, max 10 minutes per tape nightly, played numbers chalked on station door each morning. Missed or overplayed numbers requeue next night. Example: #42 plays 12 minutes, remainder returns to front of queue. **Test:** audit one week: every stub number appears once posted; shuffle-bag would show repeats and gaps.
D: **Two options:** Memorial plaque vs Seasonal salvage. **Salvage wins.** Each season's meeting walks the bridge, nominates keepable parts, then daily crossers vote for two weeks at both ends with stickers; winners are engineered into new crossing. Example: fall saves railings, cast as new balusters. **Test:** trace final fabric: salvaged parts should name commuter-chosen items, not expert picks; count sticker voters versus meeting attendees to prove daily users decided.
